paragraphs.text: Ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἐξελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῆς οἰκίας ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν·
paragraphs.translit: En tē hēmera ekeinē exelthōn ho Iēsous tēs oikias ekathēto para tēn thalassan·

i18n.en: On that day Jesus went out of the house and was sitting beside the sea.

paragraphs.text: καὶ συνήχθησαν πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλοι πολλοί, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν εἱστήκει.
paragraphs.translit: kai synēchthēsan pros auton ochloi polloi, hōste auton eis ploion embanta kathēsthai, kai pas ho ochlos epi ton aigialon heistēkei.

i18n.en: And great crowds were gathered to him, so that he got into a boat and sat down, and all the crowd stood on the shore.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς πολλὰ ἐν παραβολαῖς λέγων· Ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων τοῦ σπείρειν.
paragraphs.translit: kai elalēsen autois polla en parabolais legōn· Idou exēlthen ho speirōn tou speirein.

i18n.en: And he spoke to them many things in parables, saying: "Behold, the sower went out to sow.

paragraphs.commentary: **The Parable of the Sower opens** — one of the three major Raëlian-canon engagement sites in the Matthew translation. *Idou exēlthen ho speirōn tou speirein* — 'behold, the sower went out to sow' (generic-article *ho speirōn* = 'the sower', deliberate-typifying). Three reading-strata preserved without surface-adjudication: (1) the mainstream-Christian-traditional reception-of-the-Word reading; (2) the Jewish-historical-critical 1st-c. Galilean-Jewish agrarian-Sitz reading (Snodgrass 2008; Levine 2014); (3) the Raëlian-canon literal-soil-types-as-planet-types panspermia reading (Raël, *The Role of Christ* 1979). The WoH-Translation acknowledges-without-endorsing the Raëlian-canon citation per the Shi'ur Qomah / Qur'an / Exodus precedents. See `parable-of-the-sower-mt-13-3-23-raelian-panspermia-canon-citation-cross-corpus-with-disavowals`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐν τῷ σπείρειν αὐτὸν ἃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ ἐλθόντα τὰ πετεινὰ κατέφαγεν αὐτά.
paragraphs.translit: kai en tō speirein auton ha men epesen para tēn hodon, kai elthonta ta peteina katephagen auta.

i18n.en: And as he sowed, some seeds fell beside the path, and the birds came and devoured them.

paragraphs.commentary: First soil-type: *para tēn hodon* (along the path). Standard reading: seed-eaten-by-birds, allegorized at v.19 as 'the evil one' snatching the word.

paragraphs.text: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη ὅπου οὐκ εἶχεν γῆν πολλήν, καὶ εὐθέως ἐξανέτειλεν διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βάθος γῆς.
paragraphs.translit: alla de epesen epi ta petrōdē hopou ouk eichen gēn pollēn, kai eutheōs exaneteilen dia to mē echein bathos gēs.

i18n.en: Others fell on rocky ground where they did not have much soil, and immediately they sprang up, because they had no depth of soil.

paragraphs.commentary: Second soil-type: *epi ta petrōdē* (on rocky-ground). Sprung-up-quickly-but-withered for lack of root.

paragraphs.text: ἡλίου δὲ ἀνατείλαντος ἐκαυματίσθη καὶ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη.
paragraphs.translit: hēliou de anateilantos ekaumatisthē kai dia to mē echein rhizan exēranthē.

i18n.en: But when the sun rose, they were scorched, and because they had no root, they withered away.

paragraphs.text: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰς ἀκάνθας, καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ ἀπέπνιξαν αὐτά.
paragraphs.translit: alla de epesen epi tas akanthas, kai anebēsan hai akanthai kai apepnixan auta.

i18n.en: Others fell upon the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked them.

paragraphs.commentary: Third soil-type: *epi tas akanthas* (among thorns). Choked.

paragraphs.text: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν καὶ ἐδίδου καρπόν, ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.
paragraphs.translit: alla de epesen epi tēn gēn tēn kalēn kai edidou karpon, ho men hekaton ho de hexēkonta ho de triakonta.

i18n.en: And others fell upon the good soil and bore fruit, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.

paragraphs.commentary: Fourth soil-type: *epi tēn gēn tēn kalēn* (on the good soil). Thirty/sixty/hundredfold yields — extraordinarily high; Palestinian average ~7-10:1 per agrarian-historical scholarship; Pliny *NH* 18.94-95 reports up to 100:1 only in exceptional Babylonian conditions. The hundredfold-yield echoes Gen 26:12 (Isaac's hundredfold harvest at Gerar).

paragraphs.text: ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω.
paragraphs.translit: ho echōn ōta akouetō.

i18n.en: Whoever has ears, let him hear."

paragraphs.text: Καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Διὰ τί ἐν παραβολαῖς λαλεῖς αὐτοῖς;
paragraphs.translit: Kai proselthontes hoi mathētai eipan autō· Dia ti en parabolais laleis autois?

i18n.en: And the disciples came and said to him: "Why do you speak to them in parables?"

paragraphs.commentary: **The parable-purpose intercalation** (vv.10-17). The disciples ask why-Jesus-speaks-in-parables. Matthew's redactional pattern softens Mark's harsh *hina*-purpose-clause to a *hoti*-causal-clause at v.13 (see v.13 commentary).

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ὑμῖν δέδοται γνῶναι τὰ μυστήρια τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἐκείνοις δὲ οὐ δέδοται.
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen autois hoti Hymin dedotai gnōnai ta mystēria tēs basileias tōn ouranōn, ekeinois de ou dedotai.

i18n.en: And he answered and said to them: "To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of the heavens, but to them it has not been given.

paragraphs.commentary: *hymin dedotai gnōnai ta mystēria tēs basileias tōn ouranōn* — 'to you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of the heavens'. The Matthean-distinctive kingdom-formula. *mystēria* (mysteries) — apocalyptic-revelation terminology rooted in Dan 2:18-19, 27-30 (the Daniel-mystery tradition). See `kingdom-of-heaven-basileia-tōn-ouranōn-mt-distinctive-cross-corpus-hebrew-malkhut-shamayim`.

paragraphs.text: ὅστις γὰρ ἔχει, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ καὶ περισσευθήσεται· ὅστις δὲ οὐκ ἔχει, καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπ' αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hostis gar echei, dothēsetai autō kai perisseuthēsetai· hostis de ouk echei, kai ho echei arthēsetai ap' autou.

i18n.en: For whoever has, to him more will be given, and he will have abundance; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him.

paragraphs.text: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν παραβολαῖς αὐτοῖς λαλῶ, ὅτι βλέποντες οὐ βλέπουσιν καὶ ἀκούοντες οὐκ ἀκούουσιν οὐδὲ συνίουσιν·
paragraphs.translit: dia touto en parabolais autois lalō, hoti blepontes ou blepousin kai akouontes ouk akouousin oude syniousin·

i18n.en: This is why I speak to them in parables, because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand.

paragraphs.commentary: **Matthean softening of Mark's hina-clause.** Mk 4:12 reads *hina blepontes blepōsin* ('in order that seeing they may not see' — the harsh predestinarian reading); Matthew 13:13 reads *hoti blepontes ou blepousin* ('because seeing they do not see' — the explanatory reading). The Matthean editorial-softening is part of the Matthean accommodation to a Jewish-Christian community-audience. Davies-Allison ICC 2.392-393.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἀναπληροῦται αὐτοῖς ἡ προφητεία Ἠσαΐου ἡ λέγουσα· Ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε, καὶ βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε.
paragraphs.translit: kai anaplēroutai autois hē prophēteia Ēsaiou hē legousa· Akoē akousete kai ou mē synēte, kai blepontes blepsete kai ou mē idēte.

i18n.en: And in them is being fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah which says: "Hearing you will hear and not understand, and seeing you will see and not perceive.

paragraphs.commentary: **Isa 6:9-10 LXX citation.** Matthew explicitly cites the Isa 6:9-10 LXX prophetic-hardening text. **Lens-discipline:** the Isa 6:9-10 citation is an INTERNAL-Israelite prophet's lament — NOT an ethnic indictment of Jewish unbelief, and must NOT be deployed in Christian-anti-Judaic supersessionist reading. Davies-Allison ICC 2.393-395; Levine-Brettler JANT 2017 ad loc.

paragraphs.text: ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου, καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν βαρέως ἤκουσαν, καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν ἐκάμμυσαν· μήποτε ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν ἀκούσωσιν καὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ συνῶσιν καὶ ἐπιστρέψωσιν, καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: epachynthē gar hē kardia tou laou toutou, kai tois ōsin bareōs ēkousan, kai tous ophthalmous autōn ekammysan· mēpote idōsin tois ophthalmois kai tois ōsin akousōsin kai tē kardia synōsin kai epistrepsōsin, kai iasomai autous.

i18n.en: For the heart of this people has grown dull, and with their ears they barely heard, and they have closed their eyes — lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn, and I should heal them."

paragraphs.text: ὑμῶν δὲ μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ὅτι βλέπουσιν, καὶ τὰ ὦτα ὑμῶν ὅτι ἀκούουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: hymōn de makarioi hoi ophthalmoi hoti blepousin, kai ta ōta hymōn hoti akouousin.

i18n.en: But blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear.

paragraphs.text: ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ δίκαιοι ἐπεθύμησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν, καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν.
paragraphs.translit: amēn gar legō hymin hoti polloi prophētai kai dikaioi epethymēsan idein ha blepete kai ouk eidan, kai akousai ha akouete kai ouk ēkousan.

i18n.en: For amen I say to you, many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it.

paragraphs.text: Ὑμεῖς οὖν ἀκούσατε τὴν παραβολὴν τοῦ σπείραντος.
paragraphs.translit: Hymeis oun akousate tēn parabolēn tou speirantos.

i18n.en: You therefore, hear the parable of the sower.

paragraphs.commentary: **The allegorical interpretation** (vv.18-23). The Matthean Jesus' explicit interpretation of the four soil-types as the four reception-types of the Word. The interpretation is widely treated as either (a) substantially-authentic Jesus-tradition (Snodgrass 2008) or (b) early-community elaboration (Jeremias 1972).

paragraphs.text: παντὸς ἀκούοντος τὸν λόγον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ μὴ συνιέντος, ἔρχεται ὁ πονηρὸς καὶ ἁρπάζει τὸ ἐσπαρμένον ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν σπαρείς.
paragraphs.translit: pantos akouontos ton logon tēs basileias kai mē synientos, erchetai ho ponēros kai harpazei to esparmenon en tē kardia autou· houtos estin ho para tēn hodon spareis.

i18n.en: When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what has been sown in his heart; this is the one sown beside the path.

paragraphs.commentary: *ho ponēros* — 'the evil one' (masculine-article; cf. Mt 6:13). The first-soil-type allegorical-meaning: the evil-one snatching the word.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ εὐθὺς μετὰ χαρᾶς λαμβάνων αὐτόν·
paragraphs.translit: ho de epi ta petrōdē spareis, houtos estin ho ton logon akouōn kai euthys meta charas lambanōn auton·

i18n.en: And the one sown on the rocky ground — this is the one who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy,

paragraphs.text: οὐκ ἔχει δὲ ῥίζαν ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἀλλὰ πρόσκαιρός ἐστιν, γενομένης δὲ θλίψεως ἢ διωγμοῦ διὰ τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς σκανδαλίζεται.
paragraphs.translit: ouk echei de rhizan en heautō alla proskairos estin, genomenēs de thlipseōs ē diōgmou dia ton logon euthys skandalizetai.

i18n.en: yet has no root in himself but is temporary, and when tribulation or persecution arises on account of the word, he immediately falls away.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ ἡ μέριμνα τοῦ αἰῶνος καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου συμπνίγει τὸν λόγον, καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eis tas akanthas spareis, houtos estin ho ton logon akouōn kai hē merimna tou aiōnos kai hē apatē tou ploutou sympnigei ton logon, kai akarpos ginetai.

i18n.en: And the one sown into the thorns — this is the one who hears the word, and the anxiety of the age and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and he becomes unfruitful.

paragraphs.commentary: *hē merimna tou aiōnos kai hē apatē tou ploutou* — 'the anxiety of the age and the deceitfulness of wealth'. Cross-corpus to the Mt 6:25 *mē merimnate* anxiety-warning and the Mt 6:24 *mamōnas* wealth-warning — the SM-themes return in the parable's interpretation.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν καλὴν γῆν σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ συνιείς, ὃς δὴ καρποφορεῖ καὶ ποιεῖ ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.
paragraphs.translit: ho de epi tēn kalēn gēn spareis, houtos estin ho ton logon akouōn kai syniēis, hos dē karpophorei kai poiei ho men hekaton ho de hexēkonta ho de triakonta.

i18n.en: But the one sown on the good soil — this is the one who hears the word and understands it, who indeed bears fruit and yields, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.

paragraphs.text: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ σπείραντι καλὸν σπέρμα ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Allēn parabolēn parethēken autois legōn· Hōmoiōthē hē basileia tōn ouranōn anthrōpō speiranti kalon sperma en tō agrō autou.

i18n.en: He set before them another parable, saying: "The kingdom of the heavens has been likened to a man who sowed good seed in his field.

paragraphs.commentary: **The Parable of the Tares.** *allēn parabolēn parethēken autois legōn; hōmoiōthē hē basileia tōn ouranōn anthrōpō speiranti kalon sperma en tō agrō autou* — 'the kingdom of the heavens has been likened to a man who sowed good seed in his field'. The kingdom-similitude formula introduces the second of the seven Mt 13 kingdom-parables. Synoptic without parallel in Mark/Luke (uniquely Matthean).

paragraphs.text: ἐν δὲ τῷ καθεύδειν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἦλθεν αὐτοῦ ὁ ἐχθρὸς καὶ ἐπέσπειρεν ζιζάνια ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σίτου καὶ ἀπῆλθεν.
paragraphs.translit: en de tō katheudein tous anthrōpous ēlthen autou ho echthros kai epespeiren zizania ana meson tou sitou kai apēlthen.

i18n.en: But while the men slept, his enemy came and sowed darnel-weeds among the wheat and went away.

paragraphs.text: ὅτε δὲ ἐβλάστησεν ὁ χόρτος καὶ καρπὸν ἐποίησεν, τότε ἐφάνη καὶ τὰ ζιζάνια.
paragraphs.translit: hote de eblastēsen ho chortos kai karpon epoiēsen, tote ephanē kai ta zizania.

i18n.en: But when the blade sprouted and bore fruit, then the darnel also appeared.

paragraphs.text: προσελθόντες δὲ οἱ δοῦλοι τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου εἶπον αὐτῷ· Κύριε, οὐχὶ καλὸν σπέρμα ἔσπειρας ἐν τῷ σῷ ἀγρῷ; πόθεν οὖν ἔχει ζιζάνια;
paragraphs.translit: proselthontes de hoi douloi tou oikodespotou eipon autō· Kyrie, ouchi kalon sperma espeiras en tō sō agrō? pothen oun echei zizania?

i18n.en: And the householder's slaves came and said to him: "Master, did you not sow good seed in your field? Where then has it got darnel?"

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτοῖς· Ἐχθρὸς ἄνθρωπος τοῦτο ἐποίησεν. οἱ δὲ δοῦλοι λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Θέλεις οὖν ἀπελθόντες συλλέξωμεν αὐτά;
paragraphs.translit: ho de ephē autois· Echthros anthrōpos touto epoiēsen. hoi de douloi legousin autō· Theleis oun apelthontes syllexōmen auta?

i18n.en: And he said to them: "An enemy has done this." And the slaves said to him: "Do you wish then that we go and gather them?"

paragraphs.text: ὁ δέ φησιν· Οὔ, μήποτε συλλέγοντες τὰ ζιζάνια ἐκριζώσητε ἅμα αὐτοῖς τὸν σῖτον·
paragraphs.translit: ho de phēsin· Ou, mēpote syllegontes ta zizania ekrizōsēte hama autois ton siton·

i18n.en: But he said: "No, lest in gathering the darnel you uproot the wheat together with it.

paragraphs.text: ἄφετε συναυξάνεσθαι ἀμφότερα μέχρι τοῦ θερισμοῦ· καὶ ἐν καιρῷ τοῦ θερισμοῦ ἐρῶ τοῖς θερισταῖς· Συλλέξατε πρῶτον τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ δήσατε αὐτὰ εἰς δέσμας πρὸς τὸ κατακαῦσαι αὐτά, τὸν δὲ σῖτον συναγάγετε εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην μου.
paragraphs.translit: aphete synauxanesthai amphotera mechri tou therismou· kai en kairō tou therismou erō tois theristais· Syllexate prōton ta zizania kai dēsate auta eis desmas pros to katakausai auta, ton de siton synagagete eis tēn apothēkēn mou.

i18n.en: Let both grow together until the harvest; and at harvest time I will tell the reapers, 'Gather first the darnel and bind it into bundles to be burned, but gather the wheat into my barn.'"

paragraphs.text: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃν λαβὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔσπειρεν ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Allēn parabolēn parethēken autois legōn· Homoia estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn kokkō sinapeōs, hon labōn anthrōpos espeiren en tō agrō autou·

i18n.en: He set before them another parable, saying: "The kingdom of the heavens is like a mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his field,

paragraphs.commentary: **The Parable of the Mustard Seed.** *kokkō sinapeōs* — the mustard-seed parable. Cross-corpus to Dan 4:10-12 (Nebuchadnezzar's tree-vision) and Ezek 17:23 / Ezek 31:6 (the eschatological-tree-sheltering-birds image). The Matthean kingdom-formula again.

paragraphs.text: ὃ μικρότερον μέν ἐστιν πάντων τῶν σπερμάτων, ὅταν δὲ αὐξηθῇ μεῖζον τῶν λαχάνων ἐστὶν καὶ γίνεται δένδρον, ὥστε ἐλθεῖν τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ κατασκηνοῦν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ho mikroteron men estin pantōn tōn spermatōn, hotan de auxēthē meizon tōn lachanōn estin kai ginetai dendron, hōste elthein ta peteina tou ouranou kai kataskēnoun en tois kladois autou.

i18n.en: which is the smallest of all seeds, but when it has grown is greater than the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches.

paragraphs.text: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς· Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ζύμῃ, ἣν λαβοῦσα γυνὴ ἐνέκρυψεν εἰς ἀλεύρου σάτα τρία ἕως οὗ ἐζυμώθη ὅλον.
paragraphs.translit: Allēn parabolēn elalēsen autois· Homoia estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn zymē, hēn labousa gynē enekrypsen eis aleurou sata tria heōs hou ezymōthē holon.

i18n.en: He spoke to them another parable: "The kingdom of the heavens is like leaven that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until it was all leavened."

paragraphs.commentary: **The Parable of the Leaven.** Surprising: *zymē* (leaven) standardly carries negative-symbolism in Jewish-tradition (Ex 12:15-20 unleavened-bread; Mt 16:6 'beware of the leaven of the Pharisees'); the kingdom-as-leaven inverts the standard symbolism. Davies-Allison ICC 2.422-424.

paragraphs.text: ταῦτα πάντα ἐλάλησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν παραβολαῖς τοῖς ὄχλοις, καὶ χωρὶς παραβολῆς οὐδὲν ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς·
paragraphs.translit: tauta panta elalēsen ho Iēsous en parabolais tois ochlois, kai chōris parabolēs ouden elalei autois·

i18n.en: All these things Jesus spoke to the crowds in parables, and without a parable he spoke nothing to them,

paragraphs.text: ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Ἀνοίξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὸ στόμα μου, ἐρεύξομαι κεκρυμμένα ἀπὸ καταβολῆς.
paragraphs.translit: hopōs plērōthē to rhēthen dia tou prophētou legontos· Anoixō en parabolais to stoma mou, ereuxomai kekrymmena apo katabolēs.

i18n.en: so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying: "I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter what has been hidden from the foundation."

paragraphs.commentary: Citation of Ps 78:2 LXX *anoixō en parabolais to stoma mou ereuxomai kekrymmena apo katabolēs* ('I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter what has been hidden from the foundation of the world'). The Matthean *hina plērōthē* fulfillment-formula again. Davies-Allison ICC 2.425-426.

paragraphs.text: Τότε ἀφεὶς τοὺς ὄχλους ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν. καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Διασάφησον ἡμῖν τὴν παραβολὴν τῶν ζιζανίων τοῦ ἀγροῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Tote apheis tous ochlous ēlthen eis tēn oikian. kai prosēlthon autō hoi mathētai autou legontes· Diasaphēson hēmin tēn parabolēn tōn zizaniōn tou agrou.

i18n.en: Then leaving the crowds, he went into the house. And his disciples came to him, saying: "Explain to us the parable of the darnel of the field."

paragraphs.commentary: Transition to the indoor allegorical-interpretation of the Tares. The audience-shift (crowds → disciples) parallels the structure of the Sower-parable + interpretation.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ὁ σπείρων τὸ καλὸν σπέρμα ἐστὶν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen· Ho speirōn to kalon sperma estin ho huios tou anthrōpou·

i18n.en: And he answered and said: "The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man.

paragraphs.commentary: *ho speirōn to kalon sperma estin ho huios tou anthrōpou* — 'the one sowing the good seed is the Son of Man'. The Son-of-Man identification (cf. Dan 7:13-14; Mt 25:31) — see `son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ ἀγρός ἐστιν ὁ κόσμος· τὸ δὲ καλὸν σπέρμα, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τῆς βασιλείας· τὰ δὲ ζιζάνιά εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ πονηροῦ,
paragraphs.translit: ho de agros estin ho kosmos· to de kalon sperma, houtoi eisin hoi huioi tēs basileias· ta de zizania eisin hoi huioi tou ponērou,

i18n.en: The field is the world; the good seed — these are the sons of the kingdom; the darnel are the sons of the evil one,

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ ἐχθρὸς ὁ σπείρας αὐτά ἐστιν ὁ διάβολος· ὁ δὲ θερισμὸς συντέλεια αἰῶνός ἐστιν, οἱ δὲ θερισταὶ ἄγγελοί εἰσιν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de echthros ho speiras auta estin ho diabolos· ho de therismos synteleia aiōnos estin, hoi de theristai angeloi eisin.

i18n.en: and the enemy who sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the consummation of the age, and the reapers are angels.

paragraphs.text: ὥσπερ οὖν συλλέγεται τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ πυρὶ κατακαίεται, οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος.
paragraphs.translit: hōsper oun syllegetai ta zizania kai pyri katakaietai, houtōs estai en tē synteleia tou aiōnos.

i18n.en: Therefore as the darnel is gathered and burned with fire, so it shall be at the consummation of the age.

paragraphs.text: ἀποστελεῖ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ, καὶ συλλέξουσιν ἐκ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ σκάνδαλα καὶ τοὺς ποιοῦντας τὴν ἀνομίαν,
paragraphs.translit: apostelei ho huios tou anthrōpou tous angelous autou, kai syllexousin ek tēs basileias autou panta ta skandala kai tous poiountas tēn anomian,

i18n.en: The Son of Man will send out his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom all causes of offense and those who do lawlessness,

paragraphs.commentary: *apostelei ho huios tou anthrōpou tous angelous autou* — 'the Son of Man will send his angels'. Apocalyptic-judgment scene; the Son-of-Man-with-his-angels echoes Dan 7:10 + Mt 25:31. See `son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
paragraphs.translit: kai balousin autous eis tēn kaminon tou puros· ekei estai ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn.

i18n.en: and will throw them into the furnace of fire; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.

paragraphs.commentary: *tēn kaminon tou pyros; ekei estai ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn* — 'the furnace of fire; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth'. Apocalyptic-judgment imagery rooted in 1 Enoch 90:24-27 + Jub 24:30 + Dan 3:6 (Nebuchadnezzar's furnace). The 'weeping and gnashing of teeth' is a Matthean-distinctive formula (6x in Matthew + Lk 13:28).

paragraphs.text: τότε οἱ δίκαιοι ἐκλάμψουσιν ὡς ὁ ἥλιος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν. ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω.
paragraphs.translit: tote hoi dikaioi eklampsousin hōs ho hēlios en tē basileia tou patros autōn. ho echōn ōta akouetō.

i18n.en: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Whoever has ears, let him hear.

paragraphs.text: Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν θησαυρῷ κεκρυμμένῳ ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ, ὃν εὑρὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔκρυψεν, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς αὐτοῦ ὑπάγει καὶ πωλεῖ πάντα ὅσα ἔχει καὶ ἀγοράζει τὸν ἀγρὸν ἐκεῖνον.
paragraphs.translit: Homoia estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn thēsaurō kekrymmenō en tō agrō, hon heurōn anthrōpos ekrypsen, kai apo tēs charas autou hypagei kai pōlei panta hosa echei kai agorazei ton agron ekeinon.

i18n.en: The kingdom of the heavens is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and hid; and from joy over it he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.

paragraphs.commentary: **The Parable of the Hidden Treasure.** Brief-vivid parable contrasting the discovery's joy and the all-in commitment.

paragraphs.text: Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ ἐμπόρῳ ζητοῦντι καλοὺς μαργαρίτας·
paragraphs.translit: Palin homoia estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn anthrōpō emporō zētounti kalous margaritas·

i18n.en: Again, the kingdom of the heavens is like a merchant seeking fine pearls;

paragraphs.commentary: **The Parable of the Pearl of Great Price.** Parallel structure to the Hidden Treasure. The Matthean kingdom-formula again.

paragraphs.text: εὑρὼν δὲ ἕνα πολύτιμον μαργαρίτην ἀπελθὼν πέπρακεν πάντα ὅσα εἶχεν καὶ ἠγόρασεν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: heurōn de hena polytimon margaritēn apelthōn pepraken panta hosa eichen kai ēgorasen auton.

i18n.en: and having found one pearl of great value, he went and sold all that he had and bought it.

paragraphs.text: Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν σαγήνῃ βληθείσῃ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ ἐκ παντὸς γένους συναγαγούσῃ·
paragraphs.translit: Palin homoia estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn sagēnē blētheisē eis tēn thalassan kai ek pantos genous synagagousē·

i18n.en: Again, the kingdom of the heavens is like a dragnet cast into the sea and gathering of every kind,

paragraphs.commentary: **The Parable of the Net.** The fishing-net + sorting-of-fish at the eschatological-judgment. The good-vs-bad sorting parallels the wheat-vs-tares structure of vv.24-30, 36-43.

paragraphs.text: ἣν ὅτε ἐπληρώθη ἀναβιβάσαντες ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν καὶ καθίσαντες συνέλεξαν τὰ καλὰ εἰς ἄγγη, τὰ δὲ σαπρὰ ἔξω ἔβαλον.
paragraphs.translit: hēn hote eplērōthē anabibasantes epi ton aigialon kai kathisantes synelexan ta kala eis angē, ta de sapra exō ebalon.

i18n.en: which, when it was full, they drew up onto the shore, and sitting down they gathered the good into vessels but threw the bad away.

paragraphs.text: οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος· ἐξελεύσονται οἱ ἄγγελοι καὶ ἀφοριοῦσιν τοὺς πονηροὺς ἐκ μέσου τῶν δικαίων
paragraphs.translit: houtōs estai en tē synteleia tou aiōnos· exeleusontai hoi angeloi kai aphoriousin tous ponērous ek mesou tōn dikaiōn

i18n.en: So it shall be at the consummation of the age. The angels shall go out and separate the evil from among the righteous,

paragraphs.text: καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
paragraphs.translit: kai balousin autous eis tēn kaminon tou puros· ekei estai ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn.

i18n.en: and shall throw them into the furnace of fire; there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.

paragraphs.text: Συνήκατε ταῦτα πάντα; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ναί.
paragraphs.translit: Synēkate tauta panta? legousin autō· Nai.

i18n.en: Have you understood all these things?" They said to him, "Yes."

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τοῦτο πᾶς γραμματεὺς μαθητευθεὶς τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅστις ἐκβάλλει ἐκ τοῦ θησαυροῦ αὐτοῦ καινὰ καὶ παλαιά.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autois· Dia touto pas grammateus mathēteutheis tē basileia tōn ouranōn homoios estin anthrōpō oikodespotē hostis ekballei ek tou thēsaurou autou kaina kai palaia.

i18n.en: And he said to them: "Therefore every scribe who has been discipled into the kingdom of the heavens is like a householder who brings out of his treasure things new and old."

paragraphs.commentary: *pas grammateus mathēteutheis tē basileia tōn ouranōn ... ekballei ek tou thēsaurou autou kaina kai palaia* — 'every scribe trained for the kingdom of the heavens ... brings out from his treasure new things and old'. The Matthean self-identification of the trained-scribe (treasures-old-and-new = Hebrew Bible + Jesus-tradition). The Matthean closing of the kingdom-parables discourse-block. Davies-Allison ICC 2.445-447.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς παραβολὰς ταύτας, μετῆρεν ἐκεῖθεν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai egeneto hote etelesen ho Iēsous tas parabolas tautas, metēren ekeithen.

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these parables, he departed from there.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὴν πατρίδα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ αὐτῶν, ὥστε ἐκπλήσσεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ λέγειν· Πόθεν τούτῳ ἡ σοφία αὕτη καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις;
paragraphs.translit: kai elthōn eis tēn patrida autou edidasken autous en tē synagōgē autōn, hōste ekplēssesthai autous kai legein· Pothen toutō hē sophia hautē kai hai dynameis?

i18n.en: And coming into his native town, he taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished and said: "Where did this man get this wisdom and these mighty works?

paragraphs.commentary: Transition to the Nazareth-rejection narrative. Cross-synoptic to Mk 6:1-6.

paragraphs.text: οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τοῦ τέκτονος υἱός; οὐχ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ λέγεται Μαριὰμ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωσὴφ καὶ Σίμων καὶ Ἰούδας;
paragraphs.translit: ouch houtos estin ho tou tektonos huios? ouch hē mētēr autou legetai Mariam kai hoi adelphoi autou Iakōbos kai Iōsēph kai Simōn kai Ioudas?

i18n.en: Is not this the carpenter's son? Is not his mother called Mary, and his brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?

paragraphs.text: καὶ αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ οὐχὶ πᾶσαι πρὸς ἡμᾶς εἰσιν; πόθεν οὖν τούτῳ ταῦτα πάντα;
paragraphs.translit: kai hai adelphai autou ouchi pasai pros hēmas eisin? pothen oun toutō tauta panta?

i18n.en: And are not all his sisters with us? Where then did this man get all these things?"

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐσκανδαλίζοντο ἐν αὐτῷ. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ ἔστιν προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ πατρίδι καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eskandalizonto en autō. ho de Iēsous eipen autois· Ouk estin prophētēs atimos ei mē en tē patridi kai en tē oikia autou.

i18n.en: And they took offense at him. But Jesus said to them: "A prophet is not without honor, except in his native town and in his own household."

paragraphs.commentary: *ouk estin prophētēs atimos ei mē en tē patridi autou* — 'a prophet is not without honor except in his hometown'. The aphorism is preserved across the synoptic tradition (Mk 6:4; Lk 4:24; Jn 4:44) and in the *Gospel of Thomas* 31 — multiply-attested.

paragraphs.text: καὶ οὐκ ἐποίησεν ἐκεῖ δυνάμεις πολλὰς διὰ τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk epoiēsen ekei dynameis pollas dia tēn apistian autōn.

i18n.en: And he did not do many mighty works there, because of their unbelief.
